questions.q: What's the real danger of a local terraform.tfstate file?
options: It exists only on one machine, so losing that machine means Terraform no longer knows what it created
Terraform cannot create a local state file at all
Local state files are always corrupted after one use
Local state only works with Bicep, never with Terraform
questions.explain: Local state is a single point of failure — the one record of what's actually deployed lives only on whoever ran apply.

questions.q: What is a remote backend, in Terraform terms?
options: Shared storage for the state file — Terraform Cloud, or an azurerm backend storing it as a blob in a Storage Account
A second copy of your .tf files kept as a backup
A cloud region where resources are physically located
A tool that replaces the need for a state file entirely
questions.explain: A remote backend moves the state file off one laptop and into shared storage every teammate's plan and apply can reach.

questions.q: What extra capability does a remote backend add beyond just being shared storage?
options: State locking — preventing two apply runs from touching the state file at the same time
Automatic deletion of unused resources
Free compute for running terraform apply
Automatic conversion of Terraform code into Bicep
questions.explain: Locking is what actually prevents two people from racing to rewrite the same state file and corrupting it.

questions.q: A teammate tries to run terraform apply while your apply against the same remote state is still running. What happens?
options: Terraform refuses their apply and tells them the state is locked
Both applies run simultaneously with no conflict
Their apply silently overwrites your state file
Terraform deletes the resource group to be safe
questions.explain: That refusal is state locking doing its job — it's the mechanism, not a courtesy warning.

questions.q: Why is an azurerm backend a natural fit for teams already working in Azure, per this lesson?
options: It stores the state file as a blob in an Azure Storage Account the team provisions once, up front
It requires no Azure subscription at all
It only works for resources created through the Azure Portal
It replaces the need for a resource group
questions.explain: The azurerm backend keeps state in the same cloud the resources live in, using a Storage Account set up before anything else.
